quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The re- prefix is weak. The target is the stressed second syllable, with a /j/ glide before it.
quests.explanation: The long rounded vowel sits in the stressed second syllable, preceded by /j/. The re- prefix keeps a weak vowel that is not part of this choice.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is lax with loosely rounded lips and a tongue pulled slightly forward; /uː/ is tense, high and back with tightly rounded, protruded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The prefix de- is quick. The stressed syllable begins with /s/ and opens wide.
quests.explanation: The stressed second syllable holds the open-start diphthong, spelled i_e. Prefixes like de- and re- are usually weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen to the start point: an open, ah-like beginning means /aɪ/, an eh-like beginning means /eɪ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The same weak-prefix idea, but the strong syllable now has the spread-lip vowel.
quests.explanation: Prefix and stem hold different vowels from the same pair: a weak /ɪ/ in re- and the long vowel in the stressed -peat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the corners of the mouth: they pull back for /iː/ but stay roughly neutral for /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The last syllable holds a long steady vowel, with the lips neutral.
quests.explanation: The er here is a full vowel, not a weak schwa, because the final syllable is stressed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check your lips: still and unrounded for /ɜː/, a clear oval for /ɔː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The un- prefix is the first syllable itself. Judge it: short and central.
quests.explanation: Unlike re- and de-, the prefix un- keeps a full vowel, so the first syllable holds the central vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so don't wait for a length difference. Wait for darkness (rounding) versus neutrality.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The pro- prefix is weak, so the strong vowel comes later. Half-open jaw.
quests.explanation: The weak pro- reduces to schwa, and the stressed second syllable carries the half-open vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before nasals and voiced stops /æ/ tends to lengthen while /e/ stays brief, but the jaw gap is still the deciding cue.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Four syllables. Find the stressed one, -ca-, and let it glide.
quests.explanation: An e also appears at the start, which is why the stress is specified: the glide sits in -ca-.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Time the vowel: /e/ is over quickly, while /eɪ/ carries on and ends with the tongue rising.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE STRESSED SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The -tion is weak. The target is the stressed syllable before it.
quests.explanation: The -tion ending is just /ʃn/ with no vowel of its own, so the target is the stressed syllable before it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Push the lips into a small circle for /uː/. For /ʊ/ the rounding is slack and the tongue sits lower and further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The first vowel glides upward, and the -tion ending is just /ʃn/.
quests.explanation: The -tion ending never gets a full vowel, and the stressed first syllable has the glide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The end of /eɪ/ is a tiny /ɪ/. If the word finishes with a faint 'ee', it is /eɪ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The a is long and gliding in the first syllable, and the ending is weak.
quests.explanation: The -ous ending is weak, so the stressed first syllable carries the glide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Many learners shorten /eɪ/ to /e/. Extend it and feel the jaw close.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: A wide-open first syllable, then a short weak ending.
quests.explanation: The -ive ending is weak and short, and the wide vowel is in the first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ and /æ/ differ by about one step of tongue height on the vowel chart: mid-front versus near-open front.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: In the first syllable, round the lips and keep it short.
quests.explanation: The first syllable is stressed and rounded, and the -ive ending reduces to a weak vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If /ʌ/ keeps coming out as /ɒ/, relax the lips completely and let the tongue rest in the middle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The pay- part is stressed, with a rising glide.
quests.explanation: The pay- part carries the stress, and the -ment ending is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling traps: i_e, igh and y give /aɪ/, while a_e, ai and ay give /eɪ/. Words like eight and height show the exceptions.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The open start and forward glide are in the first syllable.
quests.explanation: The nd cluster doesn't change the diphthong, which sits in the stressed first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end in a glide towards /ɪ/, but /aɪ/ starts wide open and /eɪ/ starts mid-front.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The first syllable begins wide open; the -ful ending is weak.
quests.explanation: The -ful ending is weak and short, and the wide start is in the first syllable.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both finish with lips rounding. The beginnings differ: ah-like for /aʊ/, schwa-like for /əʊ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Before dark /l/ the vowel can seem less tense. Keep the lips spread.
quests.explanation: The dark /l/ pulls the tongue back and can make the vowel sound less pure, but the lips stay spread.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Weak -ing, -ish and -ic endings carry /ɪ/ and are never lengthened. Save the long, tense vowel for stressed syllables.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A short vowel before /lk/. The tongue stays relaxed and a little low.
quests.explanation: Learners often over-tense it before the dark /l/, making 'meelk'. Keep it short and lax.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling is mixed: ee and ea usually spell /iː/, i and y spell /ɪ/ in most words, with exceptions such as 'machine'.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The vowel is short and rounded before dark /l/.
quests.explanation: Rounded lips and a quick vowel. A tense 'bool' would sound like a different word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are rounded, so rounding alone will not separate them: /uː/ is purer and longer, /ʊ/ brief and a little more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Before /ŋ/ the vowel stays short and the tongue stays lower than for 'reen'.
quests.explanation: Before /ŋ/ the vowel stays short and the tongue relaxes, so 'reeng' would be wrong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Try whispering: even without voice the difference in tongue height is audible, which shows that quality, not just length, carries the contrast.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The jaw opens wide before /ŋ/. Some nasal colour is natural.
quests.explanation: Nasals often colour the vowel, but the wide jaw stays.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling won't tell you: a gives /e/ in 'many' and /æ/ in 'cat', and ea gives /e/ in 'head'. Decide with ears and jaw.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and rounded before the nasal /ŋ/.
quests.explanation: Although it looks like 'lawn', the vowel is shorter, and the -ng does not lengthen it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue rises from open /ɒ/ to mid-high /ɔː/, and the lips tighten from a slight oval to a clear one.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Before voiceless /f/ the vowel shortens a little but stays tense.
quests.explanation: A little shorter before /f/, yet still bright and tense.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A voiceless consonant after the vowel shortens both. If duration seems to vanish, rely on the tense quality of /iː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The lips close in a glide and /p/ ends it.
quests.explanation: The o_e spelling is regular. The voiceless /p/ shortens the glide but doesn't remove it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: o_e and oa mostly spell /əʊ/, while a single o in a short closed syllable (hot, shop) is usually /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The glide is shortened by /t/ but still starts open.
quests.explanation: A clipped glide still begins with an open jaw, unlike the higher-starting one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The jaw starts lower for /aɪ/ and visibly closes. /eɪ/ starts nearly half closed and moves less.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: When r is followed by a vowel, this stressed vowel stays short.
quests.explanation: Unlike 'hurt', an r followed by a vowel usually keeps the preceding vowel short, though the ur spelling is the same.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling will not decide: ir, er, ur, ear and wor- give /ɜː/, while u, o and ou usually give /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A wide jaw. The r joins the second syllable.
quests.explanation: When r is followed by a vowel, the preceding vowel is usually short, unlike in 'car'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The contrast is clearest in stressed syllables; in weak syllables both tend to drift towards a neutral vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and rounded. The rr spelling marks a short vowel.
quests.explanation: The rr signals a short vowel. Compare 'sore', which has the long one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After the vowel, -or before a consonant (fork, short) usually means /ɔː/, while o before a stop (top, stop) means /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: The sun- part is short and central.
quests.explanation: The first part has the central vowel. The second syllable has a diphthong that is not part of this choice.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is back and open with slightly rounded lips; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded with neutral lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Oo before n is long.
quests.explanation: In compounds each part keeps its own vowel, and the first part here is long and rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The quality gap is larger than the length gap. /ʊ/ is not simply a shortened /uː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE VOWEL IN THE FIRST SYLLABLE
quests.hint: Ea is short here; the second part has a glide.
quests.explanation: The 'head' part keeps the short vowel while 'ache' glides. In compounds the two parts keep separate vowels.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A self-check: rest a hand under your chin. The jaw should drop noticeably further for /æ/.
